films.title: Within Our Gates
films.synopsis: A young Black teacher travels north to raise money for a struggling Southern school. The oldest surviving feature by an African American director, made as a direct answer to The Birth of a Nation.

films.title: The Learning Tree
films.synopsis: A teenager comes of age in 1920s Kansas, facing love, racism and a murder he witnessed. Parks adapted his own semi-autobiographical novel.

films.title: Shaft
films.synopsis: A private detective is hired by a Harlem crime boss to find his kidnapped daughter. Isaac Hayes' theme became as famous as the film.

films.title: Sweet Sweetback's Baadasssss Song
films.synopsis: After stopping two police officers from beating a young activist, a man goes on the run across Los Angeles. Made independently and defiantly, it became a box-office phenomenon.

films.title: Ganja & Hess
films.synopsis: An anthropologist is stabbed with a cursed ancient dagger and becomes addicted to blood. A hypnotic, experimental film about faith, desire and assimilation.

films.title: Killer of Sheep
films.synopsis: A slaughterhouse worker in Watts drifts through his days, numbed by work and money worries. Shot on weekends for under $10,000, it waited almost thirty years for a proper release.

films.title: Losing Ground
films.synopsis: A philosophy professor researching ecstatic experience spends a summer upstate with her painter husband, and starts to find some ecstasy of her own.

films.title: Bless Their Little Hearts
films.synopsis: An unemployed father in Watts struggles to hold on to his dignity and his family. Written and shot by Charles Burnett.

films.title: Hollywood Shuffle
films.synopsis: An aspiring actor auditions for the only roles Hollywood offers Black men: pimps, gangsters and butlers. A satire told in sketches and daydreams.

films.title: Do the Right Thing
films.synopsis: On the hottest day of the year on one Brooklyn block, tensions between neighbors, a pizzeria owner and the police build towards an explosion.

films.title: Tongues Untied
films.synopsis: Poetry, performance and testimony from Black gay men, including Riggs himself and the poet Essex Hemphill. Its broadcast on public television caused a national controversy.

films.title: To Sleep with Anger
films.synopsis: A charming old friend from the South arrives at a Los Angeles family's home and slowly turns everyone against each other.

films.title: Boyz n the Hood
films.synopsis: Three friends grow up in South Central Los Angeles, where a father's guidance is the thin line between a future and the street.

films.title: Daughters of the Dust
films.synopsis: In 1902, three generations of Gullah women gather on an island off the coast of South Carolina on the eve of migrating north. A ravishing, non-linear film about memory and inheritance.

films.title: Malcolm X
films.synopsis: The life of Malcolm X, from street hustler and prisoner to minister of the Nation of Islam and international voice for Black liberation.

films.title: Sankofa
films.synopsis: An African American model on a photo shoot at a Ghanaian slave fort is transported back in time to live as an enslaved woman on a plantation.

films.title: The Watermelon Woman
films.synopsis: A video-store clerk sets out to make a documentary about a forgotten Black actress from the 1930s credited only as 'The Watermelon Woman'.

films.title: Eve's Bayou
films.synopsis: In 1960s Louisiana, ten-year-old Eve sees something she shouldn't, and the secrets of her prosperous family begin to unravel.

films.title: Love & Basketball
films.synopsis: Two neighbors in Los Angeles fall in love with basketball, and each other, over thirteen years told in four quarters.

films.title: Pariah
films.synopsis: A Brooklyn teenager quietly embraces her identity as a lesbian, while trying to keep it hidden from her family.

films.title: Middle of Nowhere
films.synopsis: A nurse puts her life on hold while her husband serves an eight-year prison sentence, until she begins to ask what she wants for herself.

films.title: Fruitvale Station
films.synopsis: The last day in the life of Oscar Grant, a 22-year-old shot by a transit police officer in Oakland on New Year's Day, 2009.

awards.category: Un Certain Regard, Prize of the Future

films.title: 12 Years a Slave
films.synopsis: Solomon Northup, a free Black man in New York, is kidnapped in 1841 and sold into slavery in Louisiana. Based on his own memoir.

films.title: Selma
films.synopsis: Martin Luther King Jr. and the civil rights movement campaign for voting rights with a march from Selma to Montgomery, Alabama, in 1965.

films.title: 13th
films.synopsis: How the 13th Amendment's exception for criminal punishment helped turn mass incarceration into a continuation of slavery.

films.title: Moonlight
films.synopsis: Three chapters in the life of Chiron, growing up in Miami: as a boy, a teenager and a man, searching for tenderness in a world that offers little.

films.title: Get Out
films.synopsis: A young Black photographer visits his white girlfriend's family for the weekend, and their welcome turns out to be far too warm.

films.title: Mudbound
films.synopsis: Two families, one white and one Black, work the same land in the Mississippi Delta after the Second World War, as two returning veterans form a dangerous friendship.

films.title: Black Panther
films.synopsis: T'Challa returns home to the hidden, technologically advanced African nation of Wakanda to take the throne, and faces a challenger with a claim of his own.

films.title: If Beale Street Could Talk
films.synopsis: In 1970s Harlem, a young woman fights to free her fiancé, falsely accused of a crime, before their child is born. Adapted from James Baldwin's novel.

films.title: Sorry to Bother You
films.synopsis: An Oakland telemarketer discovers that using his 'white voice' unlocks success, and a corporate conspiracy stranger than he could imagine.

films.title: Hale County This Morning, This Evening
films.synopsis: An impressionistic portrait of two young men and their community in Alabama's Black Belt, assembled from five years of footage.

awards.category: Special Jury Award for Creative Vision

films.title: Us
films.synopsis: A family's beach vacation is shattered when a group of doppelgängers appears in their driveway.

films.title: Clemency
films.synopsis: A prison warden who has overseen many executions confronts the toll of her job as she prepares to execute another man.

films.title: Time
films.synopsis: Fox Rich fights for two decades for the release of her husband, sentenced to sixty years in prison, told through her own home videos.

films.title: Judas and the Black Messiah
films.synopsis: An FBI informant infiltrates the Illinois Black Panther Party and its charismatic young chairman, Fred Hampton.

films.title: A Thousand and One
films.synopsis: A mother takes her six-year-old son from the foster system, and they build a life together in a rapidly changing New York.

films.title: Hair Love
films.synopsis: A father tries to do his daughter's hair for the first time, for a very important day.

films.title: Borom Sarret
films.synopsis: A day in the life of a cart driver in Dakar. Often called the first film made in sub-Saharan Africa by a Black African director.

films.title: Black Girl
films.synopsis: A young Senegalese woman moves to the French Riviera to work for a white family and finds herself trapped, isolated and treated as a servant.

films.title: Badou Boy
films.synopsis: A mischievous street kid is chased across Dakar by a hapless policeman.

films.title: Soleil Ô
films.synopsis: An African accountant arrives in Paris full of hope, and runs into the racism of a country that calls him its child.

films.title: Sambizanga
films.synopsis: In 1961, as the Angolan liberation war begins, a woman searches the prisons of Luanda for her husband, an activist arrested by the Portuguese.

films.title: Touki Bouki
films.synopsis: A cowherd and a student dream of escaping Dakar for Paris, and scheme to raise the money. A wild, dazzling road movie that never leaves home.

films.title: Xala
films.synopsis: A wealthy businessman takes a third wife on the day of independence, only to be struck by a curse of impotence. A biting satire of the new elite.

films.title: Sugar Cane Alley
films.synopsis: In 1930s Martinique, a boy raised by his grandmother on a sugar plantation sees education as his way out.

films.title: Yeelen
films.synopsis: A young man with magical powers sets out across Mali to confront his father, a sorcerer determined to destroy him. Drawn from Bambara oral tradition.

films.title: Tilaï
films.synopsis: A man returns to his village to find that his father has married the woman he loved. Their affair breaks a law that cannot be broken.

films.title: Hyenas
films.synopsis: A woman who left her village in disgrace returns rich beyond measure and offers a fortune for the death of the man who wronged her. Based on Dürrenmatt's The Visit.

films.title: Quartier Mozart
films.synopsis: A schoolgirl in a Yaoundé neighborhood is transformed by a sorceress into a young man, to learn how the other half lives.

films.title: Moolaadé
films.synopsis: A woman in a Burkinabé village offers protection to four girls fleeing ritual cutting, defying the elders. Sembène's final film.

films.title: Bamako
films.synopsis: In a courtyard in Mali's capital, a trial is staged: African society against the World Bank and the IMF, while daily life goes on around it.

films.title: The Figurine
films.synopsis: Two friends find a mysterious statue in an abandoned shrine, and their fortunes change for seven years. A landmark of New Nollywood.

films.title: A Screaming Man
films.synopsis: A former swimming champion who works as a pool attendant at a hotel in N'Djamena loses his job to his own son as civil war closes in.

films.title: Timbuktu
films.synopsis: A cattle herder and his family live peacefully in the dunes outside Timbuktu, as jihadists occupy the city and ban music, laughter and football.

films.title: Félicité
films.synopsis: A proud bar singer in Kinshasa races across the city to raise money for her son's operation after a motorcycle accident.

films.title: I Am Not a Witch
films.synopsis: After a minor incident in her village, a nine-year-old girl is accused of witchcraft and sent to a witch camp, where she is tied to a spool of white ribbon.

awards.category: Outstanding Debut by a British Writer, Director or Producer

films.title: Rafiki
films.synopsis: Two young women in Nairobi, whose fathers are political rivals, fall in love in a society that forbids it. The first Kenyan film selected for Cannes.

films.title: Atlantics
films.synopsis: In a Dakar suburb, unpaid construction workers set out across the ocean for Spain. The women they leave behind begin to be haunted by something strange.

films.title: This Is Not a Burial, It's a Resurrection
films.synopsis: An eighty-year-old widow in a mountain village in Lesotho prepares for her own death, and then refuses to let her community be flooded for a dam.

films.title: On Becoming a Guinea Fowl
films.synopsis: Driving home from a party, a woman finds her uncle dead on the road. At his funeral, the family's long-buried secrets surface.

films.title: Dahomey
films.synopsis: Twenty-six royal treasures looted by French troops in 1892 are returned from Paris to Benin. Part documentary, part fable, narrated by one of the objects.

films.title: Pressure
films.synopsis: A British-born son of Trinidadian parents leaves school full of promise and runs into unemployment and racism, and his older brother's Black Power activism.

films.title: Handsworth Songs
films.synopsis: Made by the Black Audio Film Collective in the wake of the 1985 riots in Birmingham and London, a poetic essay on race, migration and British history.

films.title: Looking for Langston
films.synopsis: A black-and-white meditation on Langston Hughes and the Black gay artists of the Harlem Renaissance.

films.title: The Last Angel of History
films.synopsis: A time traveler searches for the code to the future in the work of Black musicians, artists and writers. A founding text of Afrofuturism.

films.title: Lumumba
films.synopsis: The rise and assassination of Patrice Lumumba, the first prime minister of the independent Congo.

films.title: Hunger
films.synopsis: Inside the Maze prison in 1981, IRA prisoner Bobby Sands leads a hunger strike to be recognized as a political prisoner.

films.title: Belle
films.synopsis: The mixed-race great-niece of the Lord Chief Justice is raised among the English aristocracy, as a landmark case about the slave trade comes before her uncle.

films.title: I Am Not Your Negro
films.synopsis: James Baldwin's unfinished book about Medgar Evers, Malcolm X and Martin Luther King Jr., brought to the screen in his own words.

films.title: Les Misérables
films.synopsis: A new police officer joins an anti-crime unit in Montfermeil, east of Paris, and a botched arrest caught on a drone camera threatens to set the estate alight.

films.title: Saint Omer
films.synopsis: A novelist attends the trial of a young Senegalese woman accused of leaving her baby daughter on a beach to drown, and finds herself in the story.

awards.category: Lion of the Future, Best Debut

films.title: Rye Lane
films.synopsis: Two young Londoners, both reeling from bad breakups, meet in a gallery toilet and spend a day wandering South London together.

films.title: Soul in the Eye
films.synopsis: Set to John Coltrane, a wordless film in which Bulbul performs the history of the African diaspora with his own body. A founding work of Black Brazilian cinema.

people.name: Oscar Micheaux
people.bio: The most prolific Black filmmaker of the silent and early sound eras. He wrote, produced and distributed more than forty films for Black audiences.

people.name: Gordon Parks
people.bio: Photographer for Life magazine, composer and author who became the first African American to direct a major Hollywood studio feature.

people.name: Melvin Van Peebles
people.bio: Novelist, composer and filmmaker whose independent hit Sweet Sweetback's Baadasssss Song changed what Black cinema could be and who could pay for it.

people.name: Bill Gunn
people.bio: Actor, playwright, novelist and director whose experimental vampire film Ganja & Hess has grown from cult object to recognized masterpiece.

people.name: Charles Burnett
people.bio: A central figure of the L.A. Rebellion, the movement of Black filmmakers who emerged from UCLA in the 1970s. His quiet, observant films of working-class Los Angeles life are landmarks of American independent cinema.

people.name: Kathleen Collins
people.bio: Playwright, professor and filmmaker whose Losing Ground was among the first features directed by an African American woman. Largely unseen in her lifetime, it was restored and rediscovered in 2015.

people.name: Billy Woodberry
people.bio: L.A. Rebellion filmmaker whose Bless Their Little Hearts is a key work of the movement.

people.name: Robert Townsend
people.bio: Comedian, actor and director who famously financed his first feature partly on credit cards.

people.name: Spike Lee
people.bio: Brooklyn filmmaker whose 40 Acres and a Mule Filmworks has produced some of the most influential American films of the last four decades, from She's Gotta Have It to BlacKkKlansman.

people.name: Marlon Riggs
people.bio: Documentary filmmaker, poet and educator whose essay films explored Black gay identity and the images America made of Black people.

people.name: John Singleton
people.bio: South Central Los Angeles native whose debut made him the youngest person, and the first African American, nominated for the Academy Award for Best Director.

people.name: Julie Dash
people.bio: L.A. Rebellion filmmaker whose Daughters of the Dust was the first feature directed by an African American woman to receive a general theatrical release in the United States.

people.name: Haile Gerima
people.bio: Ethiopian-born filmmaker and L.A. Rebellion member who has long taught at Howard University and distributes his films independently.

people.name: Cheryl Dunye
people.bio: Liberian-born American filmmaker whose debut, The Watermelon Woman, is considered the first feature directed by a Black lesbian.

people.name: Kasi Lemmons
people.bio: Actor turned director whose debut, Eve's Bayou, is a landmark of Southern Gothic filmmaking.

people.name: Gina Prince-Bythewood
people.bio: Writer-director known for romantic dramas and action films alike, from Love & Basketball to The Woman King.

people.name: Dee Rees
people.bio: Nashville-born writer-director whose work moves between intimate coming-of-age drama and sweeping historical epic.

people.name: Ava DuVernay
people.bio: Director, writer and distributor whose work spans historical drama, documentary and television. She founded ARRAY to champion filmmakers of color and women.

people.name: Ryan Coogler
people.bio: Oakland director who moved from the intimate Fruitvale Station to global blockbusters, without losing the personal stakes at the heart of his work.

people.name: Steve McQueen
people.bio: London-born artist and Turner Prize winner who brought a sculptor's eye to feature filmmaking. 12 Years a Slave made him the first Black filmmaker to win the Academy Award for Best Picture as a producer.

people.name: Barry Jenkins
people.bio: Miami-born director known for lyrical, intimate dramas. His second feature, Moonlight, won the Academy Award for Best Picture.

people.name: Jordan Peele
people.bio: Comedian turned filmmaker who reinvented the American horror film as a vehicle for social observation.

people.name: Boots Riley
people.bio: Oakland rapper, activist and frontman of The Coup who turned to filmmaking with a surreal anti-capitalist satire.

people.name: RaMell Ross
people.bio: Photographer and filmmaker whose work reimagines how Black life in the American South is seen on screen.

people.name: Chinonye Chukwu
people.bio: Nigerian-born American filmmaker whose Clemency made her the first Black woman to win the Sundance Grand Jury Prize for drama.

people.name: Garrett Bradley
people.bio: New Orleans-based artist and filmmaker working between documentary, fiction and archive.

people.name: Shaka King
people.bio: Brooklyn writer-director whose second feature brought the story of Fred Hampton to a wide audience.

people.name: A.V. Rockwell
people.bio: Queens-born writer-director whose debut feature won the Sundance Grand Jury Prize.

people.name: Matthew A. Cherry
people.bio: Former NFL wide receiver turned filmmaker and producer.

people.name: Ousmane Sembène
people.bio: Novelist and filmmaker, widely called the father of African cinema. His films in Wolof and French dissected colonialism, corruption and patriarchy with wit and anger.

people.name: Djibril Diop Mambéty
people.bio: Senegalese filmmaker, actor and poet whose few, wildly inventive films remain among the most original in world cinema.

people.name: Med Hondo
people.bio: Mauritanian director and celebrated French voice actor whose politically charged films confronted colonialism and the immigrant experience in France.

people.name: Sarah Maldoror
people.bio: French filmmaker of Guadeloupean descent and a pioneer of African cinema, whose work was rooted in the liberation struggles of Angola and Guinea-Bissau.

people.name: Euzhan Palcy
people.bio: Martinican director who became the first Black woman to direct a film for a major Hollywood studio, and an honorary Oscar recipient in 2022.

people.name: Souleymane Cissé
people.bio: Malian director who trained in Moscow and made some of the defining works of West African cinema.

people.name: Idrissa Ouédraogo
people.bio: Burkinabé director whose village tales, made with largely non-professional casts, won major prizes at Cannes and FESPACO.

people.name: Jean-Pierre Bekolo
people.bio: Cameroonian director whose playful, genre-bending films challenged expectations of what African cinema should look like.

people.name: Abderrahmane Sissako
people.bio: Mauritanian-born filmmaker raised in Mali, known for contemplative films about globalization and extremism in Africa.

people.name: Kunle Afolayan
people.bio: Nigerian actor, producer and director who helped lead a new wave of higher-budget Nollywood filmmaking.

people.name: Mahamat-Saleh Haroun
people.bio: Chadian director whose films about fathers, sons and civil war made him the first filmmaker from his country to compete at Cannes.

people.name: Alain Gomis
people.bio: French-Senegalese director whose films follow people at moments of crisis, in Dakar, Kinshasa and Paris.

people.name: Rungano Nyoni
people.bio: Zambian-Welsh writer-director whose darkly funny films examine tradition, family and silence.

people.name: Wanuri Kahiu
people.bio: Kenyan filmmaker and advocate of 'AfroBubbleGum', art that is fun, fierce and frivolous. Her film Rafiki was banned at home before a court lifted the ban.

people.name: Mati Diop
people.bio: French-Senegalese actor and director, niece of Djibril Diop Mambéty. Atlantics made her the first Black woman to compete for the Palme d'Or.

people.name: Lemohang Jeremiah Mosese
people.bio: Lesotho-born filmmaker and visual artist based in Berlin, known for striking, painterly compositions.

people.name: Horace Ové
people.bio: Trinidad-born British filmmaker and photographer. Pressure was the first feature by a Black director made in Britain.

people.name: John Akomfrah
people.bio: Ghanaian-born British artist and filmmaker, co-founder of the Black Audio Film Collective, known for essay films built from archive.

people.name: Isaac Julien
people.bio: London-born artist and filmmaker, co-founder of the Sankofa Film and Video Collective and a key figure in New Queer Cinema.

people.name: Raoul Peck
people.bio: Haitian filmmaker, raised partly in Congo, who has served as Haiti's Minister of Culture and has made documentaries and dramas about colonialism, power and resistance.

people.name: Amma Asante
people.bio: Former child actor turned writer-director of period dramas about race, love and power.

people.name: Ladj Ly
people.bio: Filmmaker from Montfermeil, east of Paris, and co-founder of the Kourtrajmé collective. He started by filming his own neighborhood.

people.name: Alice Diop
people.bio: French documentary filmmaker of Senegalese descent whose first fiction feature, Saint Omer, won the Grand Jury Prize at Venice.

people.name: Raine Allen-Miller
people.bio: South London director who came up through music videos and commercials before her feature debut.

people.name: Zózimo Bulbul
people.bio: Brazilian actor and filmmaker, a pioneer of Black Brazilian cinema and founder of a center for Afro-Brazilian film in Rio de Janeiro.

collections.title: The L.A. Rebellion
collections.description: In the 1970s and 80s, a group of Black students at UCLA set out to make films that had nothing to do with Hollywood. Their work, rooted in everyday Black life, reshaped American independent cinema.

collections.title: Classics of African Cinema
collections.description: From Sembène's first features to the FESPACO prizewinners of the 1980s and 90s: the films that built a cinema of independence.

collections.title: Pioneers
collections.description: The filmmakers who got there first, often with no money, no studio and no precedent.

collections.title: New Black Cinema
collections.description: The late 1980s and early 90s, when a wave of young directors brought Black stories into multiplexes across America.

collections.title: Contemporary African Cinema
collections.description: A new generation of directors from across the continent and its diaspora, winning at Cannes, Berlin and Venice.

collections.title: Black British Cinema
collections.description: From the workshop collectives of the 1980s to the present day.

collections.title: Black Queer Cinema
collections.description: Films that put Black queer lives at the center.

collections.title: Winners at Cannes
collections.description: Films that took home prizes at the Cannes Film Festival.

collections.title: Academy Award Winners
collections.description: Films that won at least one Oscar.

collections.title: Sundance Breakthroughs
collections.description: Debuts and second features that broke out at Sundance.

collections.title: Shorts & Animation
collections.description: Short films, some of them the first steps of great careers.

collections.title: Francophone Cinema
collections.description: Films from France, West and Central Africa and the Caribbean, in French and the languages spoken alongside it.
